summary: Feature request: extend Quartz to support Effect type-fitness analysis (error/requirement channel integrity).

payload.use_case: Effect policy pack needs type-level guards that AST matchers cannot provide: detecting any/unknown/never in Effect<A,E,R> channels, and verifying that failable function bodies match their declared error types.

what_works_now: `quartz symbols` lists exported variables and their declaration lines.
`quartz info` returns the declared type string of an exported symbol (e.g., Effect.Effect<string, any, never>).
`quartz at-position` returns the type at a specific source position.

gaps.gap: No command to enumerate all Effect<...> type occurrences (variables, function returns, parameters, inline expressions).
gaps.impact: Policy harness must guess candidate positions instead of asking Quartz for every Effect-typed node.

gaps.gap: No structured access to Effect type arguments (A, E, R).
gaps.impact: Harness must regex-match the expanded type string, which is brittle for nested or aliased types.

gaps.gap: No check that compares a function body's inferred error type against its declared return type.
gaps.impact: Cannot detect the most dangerous case: a function declared `Effect<A, never, R>` that internally calls `Effect.tryPromise` or `Effect.fail`.

proposed_evolution.description: Return all AST nodes whose resolved type is Effect<...> with node kind, file, line, column, and expanded type string.
Given a symbol or position, return the three type arguments of the Effect type as structured JSON: { success, error, requirement }.
For a function returning Effect<A,E,R>, verify that the body's inferred error type is assignable to E and not silently widened to any/unknown.

cases: propagatedAnyError: Effect.Effect<string, any, never> inferred from a broken dependency

next_steps: Confirm whether the proposed commands fit Quartz's architecture or if an existing command can be extended.
If accepted, implement `effect-nodes` first; it unblocks the richest policy use case.
Update the research harness to use the new Quartz commands and retire regex-based type parsing.
